title: Two strings to zero
line: Dots at −5 and 5 each stretch a string back to zero, the strings lay side by side, and both measure exactly 5.

title: Folding the number line
line: The number line folds at zero, the negative half flips over onto the positive half, and −3 lands right on top of 3.

title: Percent on a hundred grid
line: A 10×10 grid fills 37 squares, the label reads 37/100, then the decimal point hops two places left to show 0.37.

title: 25 squares become a quarter
line: Twenty-five shaded squares out of 100 slide into one of four equal 25-square blocks, so 25% turns into 1/4 before your eyes.

title: Factor tree for 360
line: 360 splits into branches, 2×180, 2×90, and onward until every leaf is prime, then the leaves drop into a row: 2³·3²·5.

title: Rectangles of dots
line: Twelve dots rearrange into 1×12, 2×6 and 3×4 rectangles, but seven dots can only ever form a single line, so 7 is prime.

title: Cancelling in pairs
line: 12/18 rewrites as 2·2·3 over 2·3·3, matching factors above and below glow and vanish in pairs, and 2/3 is left.

title: Same pie, bigger slices
line: A pie of 18 slices, 12 shaded, loses cut lines until 3 slices remain with 2 shaded, the shaded part never changing.

title: How many halves in 3
line: Three bars get chopped into halves and each piece pops with a count, reaching 6, so 3 ÷ ½ turns out to equal 3 × 2.

title: Measuring with a 2/3 ruler
line: A 2/3-long ruler marches along 4 whole bars, fitting one and a half times per bar, and the counter lands on 6 = 4 × 3/2.

title: Halving is times one half
line: Eight dots split into two piles of 4, then shrink by ×½ to 4, and 8 ÷ 2 morphs into 8 × ½.

title: Make the bottom vanish
line: (3/4) ÷ (2/5) stacks as one tall fraction, top and bottom both get multiplied by 5/2, the bottom collapses to 1 and disappears.

title: Unrolling a circle
line: A wheel of radius 1 rolls one full turn along a line, painting a track that measures out to 2π, about 6.28.

title: Circle into rectangle
line: A circle sliced into 16 wedges unzips and the wedges interlock point up, point down, into a near-rectangle r tall and πr wide.

title: Two blinking lights
line: One light blinks every 4 seconds and another every 6 on a timeline; their tick marks first line up together at 12, the LCM.

title: Biggest square tile
line: A 12×18 floor tries 2×2 and 3×3 tiles, then 6×6 tiles cover it perfectly with the fewest pieces, so the GCF is 6.

title: Factors in overlapping circles
line: 12 = 2·2·3 and 18 = 2·3·3 drop into two overlapping circles; the shared 2·3 gives GCF 6 and everything together multiplies to LCM 36.

title: Subtracting past zero
line: A marker at 20 takes 30 steps left, counting down, crosses zero without stopping, and lands on −10.

title: Coins against a bill
line: Twenty gold chips meet thirty red debt chips, they cancel in pairs and pop, and ten red chips are left over: 20 − 30 = −10.

title: Binary odometer
line: An odometer whose wheels hold only 0 and 1 counts to 15, each wheel rolling over and carrying like 9 rolling to 10.

title: Lighting up 1011
line: The digits 1011 sit over columns 8, 4, 2, 1, and the lit columns drop down and add up to 11.

title: Thirteen dots, two groupings
line: Thirteen dots group into one ten and three ones, then regroup into an eight, a four and a one, reading 13 and 1101.

title: Turning the dot rectangle
line: Three rows of five dots rotate a quarter turn into five rows of three, and the total stays 15, so 3 × 5 = 5 × 3.

title: Distributing as splitting area
line: A 4 by (5+3) rectangle gets cut by one vertical line into 4×5 and 4×3 pieces whose areas 20 and 12 add to 32.

title: Nesting number families
line: Boxes for counting numbers, whole numbers, integers, rationals and reals grow around each other while 7, 0, −2, ¾ and π drop into place.

title: Where √2 lands
line: A unit square's diagonal swings down onto the number line between 1.41 and 1.42, and zooming in never finds a fraction there.

title: Bundling sticks
line: 347 sticks bundle themselves into tens, then the tens bundle into hundreds, leaving 3 big bundles, 4 small bundles and 7 loose sticks.

title: The zero holding a place
line: Pull the zero out of 305 and the 3 slides from the hundreds column into the tens, crashing the value to 35.

title: Snapping to the nearest tick
line: A dot at 3.67 sits between ticks 3.6 and 3.7, distance arrows measure 0.07 and 0.03, and the dot snaps to 3.7.

title: Units cancelling out
line: 60 mi/hr gets multiplied by 5280 ft/1 mi and 1 hr/3600 s, matching units cross out in pairs, and 88 ft/s is left.

title: One car, two odometers
line: A car drives one mile while a miles counter creeps to 1 and a feet counter beside it races up to 5280.

title: The hidden right triangle
line: Points (1, 2) and (7, 10) sprout legs 6 and 8, squares grow on both legs, and the gap measures 10.

title: Dragging a point
line: A point wanders around the plane while its legs to a fixed point stretch and shrink and the √(Δx² + Δy²) readout updates live.

title: Hopping by thousands
line: The decimal point in 47,000,000 hops left three places at a time, the exponent jumps 3 then 6, and it reads 47 × 10⁶.

title: Plugging in 3
line: The number 3 drops into every x of 2x² − 5x + 1, then the expression collapses one step at a time down to 4.

title: Doubling a square
line: A square splits in half again and again while the label climbs 2¹, 2², 2³ up to 2⁶, counting 64 tiny pieces.

title: Adding exponents by counting
line: x³·x⁴ spells out as three x's and four x's that slide into one row of seven, so the exponents simply add to x⁷.

title: Power of a power
line: (x²)³ unpacks into three pairs of x's that merge into one row of six, showing why the exponents multiply.

title: Walking down the powers
line: 2⁴ = 16, 2³ = 8, each step down divides by 2, and the pattern keeps going past 2⁰ = 1 to 2⁻¹ = ½ and 2⁻² = ¼.

title: Crossing the fraction bar
line: x⁻³ sitting on top of a fraction slides across the bar, its minus sign falling off as it lands below as 1/x³.

title: Two equal hops to 9
line: Multiplying from 1 to 9 in two equal hops means ×3 each time, so 9^½ = 3; three hops to 8 give 2.

title: Root first, then power
line: 8^(2/3) splits into two moves, cube root 8 down to 2, then square 2 up to 4, each lighting its part of the exponent.

title: T-chart to line
line: Rows of a T-chart for y = 2x − 1 fly off the table into dots on the axes, and a line snaps through them.

title: Picking friendly x values
line: For y = (2/3)x + 1, picking x = 1 gives a messy dot off the grid, while x = −3, 0, 3 land neatly on grid corners.

title: Folding up the line
line: The line y = 2x − 4 flips every part below the x-axis upward, leaving a V with its sharp tip at (2, 0).

title: Half a sideways parabola
line: The right half of y = x² reflects across the line y = x and turns into the curve y = √x.

title: Where the curve may start
line: For y = √(x − 2), trial points at x = 0 and 1 flash red and get rejected, and the curve begins exactly at (2, 0).

title: Test point and shade
line: A dashed line y = x + 1 appears, the point (0, 0) is tested and passes, and its whole side floods with color.

title: Raining points
line: Hundreds of dots rain onto the plane, green if y < 2x − 1 and red if not, and the green ones fill one side.

title: Why the sign flips
line: Multiplying by −1 reflects the number line across zero, so 1 and 3 swap sides and 1 < 3 becomes −1 > −3.

title: Open dot, closed dot
line: For −1 ≤ x < 4 a closed dot lights at −1, an open dot at 4, and the stretch between shades in.

title: Where the line crosses
line: A dot slides along y = −2x + 6 with live coordinates, freezing at (0, 6) and (3, 0) where one coordinate hits zero.

title: Averaging the shadows
line: Points (2, 1) and (8, 5) cast shadows on both axes, each shadow's middle is found, and the two middles meet at (5, 3).

title: Two answers to 2 + 3 × 4
line: Left to right gives 20, but 2 dots plus three rows of 4 dots counts 14, which is why multiplying goes first.

title: Peeling an expression
line: 3 + 2·(8 − 5)² collapses one operation at a time, parentheses, exponent, multiply, add, each step glowing before it shrinks to 21.

title: Sorting terms by degree
line: The terms of 4x² − 7 + x⁵ + 3x shuffle into descending order and the biggest exponent glows to name the degree, 5.

title: Adding with algebra tiles
line: Tiles for 3x² + 2x − 5 and x² − 4x + 7 pour together, red and blue pairs cancel and vanish, leaving 4x² − 2x + 2.

title: Coefficients, then letters
line: In (4x)(5x²) the 4 and 5 fly together into 20 while x and x·x merge into x³, giving 20x³.

title: A rectangle of 20 tiles
line: A 4x by 5y rectangle splits into a 4 by 5 grid of little x-by-y tiles, and the count shows the area is 20xy.

title: Factor, then cancel
line: (x² − 9)/(x + 3) factors into (x − 3)(x + 3) over (x + 3), the matching factors glow and vanish, leaving x − 3.

title: Square root as a side
line: A square of area 49 shows side 7, then grows to area 50 and its side nudges just past 7, to about 7.07.

title: Pulling 6 out of √72
line: 72 tiles split into two 6×6 squares, the side length 6 steps outside the root sign, and √72 becomes 6√2.

title: Splitting into unit rates
line: A bar for 150 miles in 3 hours cuts into 3 equal pieces of 50, showing the rate is 50 miles per hour.

title: Scaling the recipe
line: 3 blue cups and 2 yellow cups double to 6 and 4, then 9 and 6, and the mixed color never changes.

title: Measuring a tree by its shadow
line: A 6 ft person casts a 4 ft shadow; the triangle stretches until its shadow is 20 ft, and the height reads 30 ft.

title: Table rows become dots
line: Rows of hours-studied and test-score pairs fly off a table into dots on axes, and a rising cloud shows the trend.

title: Hopping decimal for big numbers
line: In 7,375,000,000 the decimal point hops left nine times, a counter ticking with each hop, until it reads 7.375 × 10⁹.

title: Hopping right for tiny numbers
line: In 0.00042 the decimal point hops right four times to 4.2, and the exponent counts down to 10⁻⁴.

title: Two equal rows
line: Tiles for 2x + 6, two x-bars and six unit squares, arrange into two identical rows of x + 3, so 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3).

title: Write it all out
line: (x³y²)/(xy⁴) spreads into single letters, matching letters top and bottom cancel in pairs, and x²/y² is all that remains.

title: Arrows through parentheses
line: In 3(2x − 5) − (x − 4) arrows shoot from 3 to each term, a hidden 1 appears before the second bracket, and its signs flip.

title: Rise over run staircase
line: A staircase of steps, 3 across and 2 up, climbs the line y = (2/3)x, then a steeper line gets taller steps.

title: Spinning line, changing slope
line: A line rotates about the origin while its slope counts up from 0 to huge near vertical, then jumps negative as it tips past.

title: Start at b, then step
line: For y = −½x + 3 a dot lands at (0, 3), hops down 1 and right 2 again and again, and a line threads the dots.

title: Starting value and rate
line: A town of 1500 grows 200 a year as a dot climbs P = 200t + 1500 and a bar stacks a block each tick.

title: Turning the m and b dials
line: In y = mx + b, turning the b dial slides the line up and down, then turning m tilts it around the y-intercept.

title: Two points at distance 4
line: For |x − 3| = 4, two arrows of length 4 shoot out from 3 in both directions and land on −1 and 7.

title: V meets a flat line
line: The V of y = |x − 3| rises to meet the flat line y = 4 and crosses it at exactly two points, −1 and 7.

title: Keeping the scale level
line: A scale holds box x plus 3 weights against 5 weights; take 3 from each side, it stays level, and x = 2.

title: Letters follow the numbers
line: 3x + 2 = 11 and ax + b = c get solved side by side, every move mirrored, so the letters follow the numbers.

title: The fake solution
line: Squaring √(x + 2) = x gives 2 and −1, but the two sides' graphs cross only at 2, exposing −1 as fake.

title: Input dial, output dial
line: Turning an x dial from 0 to 5 drags a y = 3x + 1 dial along, showing which variable you pick and which responds.

title: Two number lines make a map
line: A vertical number line rotates up through zero, then a dot finds (3, −2) by walking 3 right and 2 down.

title: Phrases into symbols
line: "Five less than twice a number" breaks into phrases that morph into symbols, and "less than" swaps the order to 2x − 5.

title: Two ages growing together
line: Age bars of 30 and 10 both grow by 10 years, and the mother's bar shrinks from triple her son's to exactly double.

title: Unfolding the fence
line: A rectangle with sides w and 2w + 3 unfolds into a straight 36 ft fence that splits into six w's and 6, so w = 5.

title: Swapping nickels for dimes
line: Twelve nickels make 60¢; coins flip to dimes one by one, each adding 5¢, and five flips reach 85¢.

title: Two trains closing in
line: Dots 300 miles apart drive toward each other at 60 and 40 mph, the gap shrinking 100 each hour until they meet at hour 3.

title: The catch-up
line: A 40 mph car leaves an hour early; a 60 mph car gains 20 miles each hour and catches it at mile 120.

title: Average speed is not 50
line: A dot drives 120 miles out at 60 mph and back at 40 mph, the clock reads 5 hours, and the average is 48.

title: Interest stacking up
line: $1000 at 5% simple interest gets a same-size $50 block stacked on each year, building a straight staircase to $1250 after 5 years.

title: Seesaw of prices
line: 12 lb of $3 peanuts balance 6 lb of $9 cashews on a seesaw whose pivot sits at $5, the mixture's price per pound.

title: Three consecutive odds
line: Three dots spaced 2 apart slide along the number line until their sum ticks to 51, landing on 15, 17 and 19.

title: Two pipes, one tank
line: Pipe A adds 1/3 of a tank per hour and pipe B adds 1/6, so together the water rises half a tank an hour.

title: Shearing the parallelogram
line: The parallelogram on (3, 1) and (1, 2) slides its top edge until it becomes a rectangle, and its area stays 5, the determinant.

title: Ten times louder each step
line: A decibel dial clicks up by 10 as a sound-energy bar grows tenfold each click, the axis zooming out to keep up.

title: Two scales, one bar
line: A bar marked 0% to 100% on one edge and 0 to 80 on the other slides a marker to 35%, reading 28.

title: Ball and its graph
line: A ball thrown up from 80 ft rises and falls while its height traces h = −16t² + 64t + 80 until it lands at t = 5.

title: The velocity arrow flips
line: An arrow on a rising ball shrinks as v = 64 − 32t counts down, vanishes at the peak at t = 2, then grows pointing downward.

title: Parabola through three points
line: A parabola wiggles through different shapes until it passes through (1, 2), (2, 3) and (3, 6), settling as y = x² − 2x + 3.

title: Building the box
line: Eleven dots sort on a line, the middle one becomes the median, each half finds its own middle, and the box draws itself.

title: Arranging four books
line: Four colored books shuffle through every order in a grid, 4 choices for the first spot, then 3, 2, 1, filling exactly 24 rows.

title: Factorials explode
line: Bars for 1! through 10! grow one by one, the axis zooming out each time, until 10! towers at 3,628,800.

title: Times ten, then subtract
line: x = 0.999… and 10x = 9.999… stack up, their endless tails of 9s line up digit by digit and cancel, leaving 9x = 9.

title: Closing the gap
line: A dot jumps to 0.9, 0.99, 0.999 toward 1 as the camera zooms in each time, and no gap ever survives the next jump.

title: Three thirds
line: Three copies of 1/3 = 0.333… stack and add to 0.999…, while three pie thirds snap together into one whole pie.

title: Mean as balance point
line: Dots at 2, 3, 3, 5, 12 sit on a seesaw whose pivot slides to balance at 5, while the median stays at 3.

title: Leveling the stacks
line: Stacks of 2, 3, 3, 5 and 12 blocks pass blocks from tall to short until every stack is 5 high, the mean.

title: Sorting into stems
line: Numbers like 23, 37, 31, 45, 28 fly into rows by tens digit, ones digits line up as leaves, and it reads like a histogram.

title: Dropping numbers into circles
line: The numbers 1 to 20 drop into circles for even and multiple of 3, with 6, 12 and 18 landing in the overlap.
